title: Package packing does not guarantee dist exists
reasoning: The package exposes only built artifacts under dist for main, types, exports, bin, and published files, but the package.json only defines an ordinary build script. npm/pnpm do not automatically run arbitrary build scripts during pack or publish. From a clean checkout, or any release path that packs before manually running build, the published tarball can omit dist while package entrypoints still reference it, breaking consumers at install/runtime.
reproduction: From a clean checkout with no packages/core/dist, run `pnpm --filter @docgit/core pack --pack-destination <tmp>` and inspect the tarball; without a prepack/prepare/prepublishOnly hook, the build script is not invoked before packing.
recommendation: Wire the package lifecycle to the build, preferably with a focused `prepack` script that runs the existing build command, and verify the tarball contains the declared main/types/bin/export files.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the package test script only runs Vitest; it does not exercise package packing or published tarball contents.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a release smoke test that removes or starts without packages/core/dist, runs `pnpm --filter @docgit/core pack --pack-destination <tmp>`, extracts the tarball, and asserts dist/index.js, dist/index.d.ts, and dist/cli.js exist.
minimumFixScope: packages/core/package.json lifecycle script plus a package-pack smoke check.
